newsitem.title: USA: Venezuela up on S&P report, broader market mixed.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela up on S&P report, broader market mixed.

text.p: Venezuelan Brady bond prices rose Monday following a postive report by Standard and Poor's, but market sources said the broader market was narrowly mixed in quiet trade following the U.S. Thanksgiving Day holiday.
"Venezuela has been helped by the S&P report," said one emerging market debt source.

At 1600 EST/2100 GMT, Venezuelan DCBs VZFLL07=RR were 3/8 higher at 86-5/8 bid, the country's FLIRBs VZ6C97=RR were 1/2 firmer at 87-5/8 bid and its par bonds VZ675C20=RR were 1/4 stronger at 76-3/4 bid.

Early in the day, S&P issued a statement saying it believed that the Venezuelan government's commitment to economic reforms would release the country from its devastating banking crisis of 1994 and 1995.
It also said the country's sovereign ratings were poised to improve should reforms continue as expected.

"Standard and Poor's does not believe that the Venezuelan financial system will weigh any longer on its sovereign rating and this could allow for an eventual amelioration of the rating should broader reforms move forward," the U.S. rating agency said.
Meanwhile, sources said Ecuador's Brady bonds were mixed following news Sunday of the country's economic plan.
"The reaction has been fairly muted because the plan was pretty much as anticipated by the market," said another market source.
Ecuador's par bonds ECPARS=RR were 1/8 softer at 47-3/7 bid, while its IEBs ECIEB=RR were 3/4 stronger at 86-3/4 bid and its PDI bonds ECPDI=RR were unchanged at 60-1/4 bid.
On Sunday, Ecuadoran President Abdala Bucaram said the country will adopt a convertibility plan to begin July 1, 1997, pegging the currency at four sucres to the dollar.
Elsewhere, sources said prices were thinly mixed in extremely quiet trade with some instruments giving up recent gains on profit-taking.
Russian Vneshkonombank dollar loans RUVNUSLNS=RR were 3/8 lower at 78-1/8 bid and Bulgaria's IABs BGFLTH11=RR were 1/4 weaker at 48-1/2 bid.
"Today is one of the quietest days ever," said one emerging market debt trader at a major U.S. investment bank.
